Commentary.Commentary: 419 to win then. That score 418 would be ringing a magical bell in Windies' minds. Flashback 2003. Against Glenn McGrath. Jason Gillespie. Brett Lee. Stuart MacGill. And Andy Bichel. But that was a Test match where Windies registered the highest ever score chased down in history. Chris Gayle was there in that game. Can he revive those memories and write the script in this ODI? Let's find out in a while...

Anything left to write for the bowlers? Sadly, no. Ashley Nurse and Carlos Brathwaite ended with good figures but the latter had gone for just 4 runs in his 1st 3 overs and then had given 20 at the end of 6. So he too, has gone for a beating towards the end. Nothing much to be said about the rest. Just a day to forget.

Normally we see overs in 10s, 12s or max 14s in the death overs. But Buttler and Morgan were dealing in 20s. Overs 42-44 resulted in 65 runs and the Brits never looked back. Both players reached their centuries with Buttler even touching 150. The world record for the most sixes in an ODI innings was broken and ironically, it was Windies who set that record in the first place, just a week ago.

Morgan and Buttler got together and initially, they just saw off the silent phase cautiously. Then post the Drinks break, came the real hitting. England were 264/3 at the end of 40. Powerplay 3 alone has yielded 154/3. Ouch.

24 sixes in 300 balls. Take the average. That is almost a six every 13 deliveries. It has been a total carnage right from the word go and had the Windies not quietened the visitors post Powerplay 1, we might have even seen 500 being crossed. Bairstow and Hales gave the tourists an excellent platform with a 100-run stand but the visiting side slipped a little. England seemed to be losing their way when Hales was dismissed around the halfway mark but there was something to come. Something unreal. Surreal.

When I entered office today, my colleague Sairaj started whining, 'Sir! Please save me! England are hitting 6s after 6s!' I did not feel at that stage that we would witness anything of this sort. Three-and-a-half hours later, I am out of adjectives and my fingers are paining. Take a bow, Jos Buttler. Take a bow, Eoin Morgan. Take a bow, England. 418/6. Simply amazing.
OUT! Taken! A wicket to end the innings. Full and outside off, Stokes reaches out and looks to clear the man at long off but holes out to Shimron Hetmyer in the deep. ENGLAND FINISH ON 418/6!
Outside off, Moeen swings but misses. They sneak in a bye.
Moeen Ali is the new man in.

OUT! BOWLED! Buttler does not stay till the end. A length ball, slower in pace, 108 kph, Jos swings hard but misses and the ball hits the timber. End of a phenomenal knock. 150 from 77 balls, 13 fours and 12 sixes!

SIX! THERE IT IS! A world record. MOST SIXES IN AN ODI INNINGS - 24 - now belongs to England. Go past the earlier record of 23 by Windies themselves against England in Bridgetown a week ago! A length ball, down the leg side, Buttler swings it over mid-wicket!
Full and outside off, sliced over cover for a run.
WIDE. Full and miles outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Stokes looks to play the reverse paddle but misses.

SIX! NUMBER 23 OF THIS INNINGS - A JOINT WORLD RECORD! Can England make it their own by hitting one more? A length ball, around off, Buttler swings and swings hard, down the ground and right over the sightscreen!
Comes down the track and bashes it over mid off for a run.
Full and outside off, hammered down the ground for a couple.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. One run added to the total. 400 UP FOR ENGLAND!

A length ball around off, Stokes heaves it towards long on for a single.

A 60-BALL 100 FOR MR. JOSEPH! Call him a freak, call this a freakish innings but he is special. Joseph Charles Buttler.  Take a bow. What a knock. And he is not done yet. His second fastest hundred in this format. Gets there with a cut through the off side for a couple.

SIX! Where has this gone? Full and around middle, right in the slot, Buttler swings this into oblivion, miles over long on again!

FREE HIT time!

FOUR! 23 off the over! A fuller ball on the pads and Buttler just nonchalantly flicks this one wide of deep mid-wicket for a boundary. It was just 5-6 meters to the left of the fielder but the timing was superb on that one, thus the fielder could not reach the ball.

FOUR! Four more. No relenting here from Buttler. A short and wide ball outside off, Jos reaches out to smash that ball but in the end just places it wide of point. No fielder in the deep and that is another boundary.
SIX! This is just power! Brute power! A low full toss on middle and Buttler gets under it and smashes it over the bowler's head for a huge one. This is just plain carnage.
FOUR! The runs are flowing here. Brathwaite strays onto the pads and Buttler gets a fine edge on the leg side as he runs this down to fine leg for a boundary.

FOUR! Long off and long on have been split to precision! A full toss on middle and Buttler smashes it right back past the bowler to his right. The fielders in the deep have no chance to stop the ball.

A length ball from around the wicket, Morgan looked to come down the ground and pull it away but gets cramped for room. Eoin seemed to have gotten an inside edge onto the hips and the ball drops on the leg side. A single is stolen. It is given as a leg bye though.
One off the last ball. A fuller one outside off and Eoin can only hit it along the ground towards long off. 21 off the over. The 300 comes up for the away side.

SIX! This is turning into a riot over! A full toss on middle and Morgan gets inside the line and smashes it way over the boundary at deep backward square leg. 20 off the over so far, how much off the last ball.
FOUR! Just over! A fuller length ball outside off and Morgan gets under it to hit it over the cover fielder's head. He jumps to reach that one but fails to do so.
FOUR! 10 off the first three balls. Full toss outside off, Morgan lofts this over mid off for a boundary.
Full and wide outside off, Morgan looks to go after it but misses it.
SIX! THAT IS WHACKED OVER! Full toss on leg, Morgan dispatches it over mid-wicket for a maximum.

FOUR! This one is an edge but it is still all runs for England. A full toss outside off, Buttler looks to smash it through the covers but gets a thin outside edge that runs past the keeper for a boundary.
FOUR! How does that go for a boundary! A really full ball on middle and Jos somehow manages to get under that one and hit it away over the bowler's head for a boundary.
SIX! Smashed! No three dots in a row. A slower ball on middle and Buttler swivels and pulls it over deep square leg for a huge one.
Another dot. 2 dots in a row. Rare. Really full outside off and Buttler hits it only as far as mid off.
Really full outside off and almost a full toss if the batsman had connected. Buttler though fails to put bat on ball and the ball goes to the keeper.
Around the wicket from Brathwaite, very full on middle and Morgan pushes it away to deep mid-wicket for a single. The 100-run stand comes up.
The end of the 2nd Powerplay. Now, the fielding team can have 5 fielders outside the circle till the end.
Very full and pushed back down the ground to long on for a run by Morgan to end a 10-run over.
A fuller ball on middle and leg, Jos tries to get under it but fails to do so. The ball rolls to long on for a single.
Full toss on middle but Buttler misses out. He can only hit it as far as mid off. No single either.
Drives the next ball down the ground to long on for a single. Smart batting.

SIX! That blow the previous ball does not seem to have changed Morgan's intentions though. A slower length ball outside off by Holder and Morgan slaps it with the wind over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. Huge!
The physios run out to check Morgan. He seems to have gotten hurt by the ball that caught him near his chest. Hopefully, he will be fine to continue.

The ball runs towards the right of mid on for a single. The English skipper somehow completes the run clutching his chest.
Jason Holder to bowl now.
Comes down the track but is not quite to the pitch of the ball and ends up pushing it to cover.

OUT! That is a spectacular catch from Shimron Hetmyer! Big wicket for the Windies. Hales does not get his century. Tossed up, around middle and off, Alex gets under it and looks to hit it down the ground. For a second, it seems like the connection is great. But suddenly, out of nowhere, Shimron Hetmyer races to his left from long on, like a spring chicken, leaps to his left and takes a stunning catch, with the ropes just behind! And then the reaction - what a swagger. Just throws the ball back into play as if to say, okay, I have taken the catch, let's move ahead.

OUT! Caught behind! There is a thin nick and Root has to depart! Second wicket for the Windies and this has come in reasonably quick time. Short and outside off, Root looked to cut but missed. There seemed to be a sound as the ball went past the bat and Shai Hope immediately started to celebrate once he took it. But umpire Oxenford shook his head. Hope immediately signalled to Holder to go for the review and one look in Snickometer was enough. A spike was generated when the ball went past the edge. On his bike, goes Joe. England maintain their approach of going after the bowling.
Caught behind? Shai Hope certainly feels so. The bowler is confident too. Let us see what the Snicko says.

Fuller on off, Jonny defends it classically off his front foot.
Bishoo starts with a flighted delivery on the pads. Hales tucks it away to the on side for a single.
Devandra Bishoo already introduced into the attack.
Follows the maximum with a clean freont foot defense.
SIX! Bairstow takes the aerial route. Tossed up delivery outside off. Jonny sees the width on offer, frees his arm and lofts it over the long off fence for a maximum.
Nurse lands it on middle and leg, Bairstow hits it straight to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Tossed up on middle and off, Jonny taps it back to the bowler.
On the pads this time by Nurse, Bairstow tucks it towards square leg and gets a brace.
Starts with a flighted delivery on off, Bairstow pushes it to mid off.
Ashley Nurse replaces his skipper.

SIX! This one is out of here. Back of a length delivery on middle and off. Hales rocks onto his back foot and heaves it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum. The ball goes three rows back for the first six of the day.
Edge but safe. Length delivery just outside off, Hales has a poke at it with soft hands and the ball falls short of the diving Chris Gayle at first slip.
Alex defends it from within the crease.

This is even better. Full length delivery on off, Bairstwo gets on his front foot and drives it through covers. Jason Holder gives it a chase and does well to stop the ball from going to the fence. The batsmen come back for the third.
Good shot. Good length delivery on off, Bairstwo drives it through covers. He does not time it well but gets a couple.
Length delivery on the stumps, Jonny defends it off his back foot.
No, he cannot. Length delivery outside off, Bairstow guides it towards third man and keeps the strike.

FOUR! Make it three-in-three. Full length delivery on off and middle, Bairstow hits it over the bowlers head. Carlos Braithwaite gives it a chase but comes second and the ball goes to the fence. Can he make it four in a row?
FOUR! This is even better. Length delivery outside off, Bairstow waits for it and cuts it through backward point for another boundary.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Good length delivery on off, Bairstow picks the length early and rocks onto his back foot. He keeps his balance and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman
Good length delivery on middle, Bairstow looks to defend but it goes to the leg side off the inner half of the bat and they take a couple.
Good length delivery on the fourth stump line. Hales does not disturb it and lets it go.
On the pads this time, Jonny tucks it away towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Slightly fuller on middle and leg, Bairstow hits it to the fielder at mid on.
Good length delivery on off, Jonny pushes it to the fielder at point.

Length delivery just outside off, Bairstow looks to run it down to third man but misses and the ball goes past the outside edge and to the keeper. There is a half-hearted appeal from the keeper bu the umpire is not interested.

Good shot and excellent fielding. Full length delivery on off, Bairstow drives it through cover but Bravo there dives to his left and saves a certain boundary. The batsman are not able to get a single either.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Hales flicks it through mid-wicket and gets a couple to finish off the over.
Wide! Holder misses his line and bowls this down the leg side. Hales looks to flick it but misses. The umpire signals it as wide.
Holder lands it on a length and Hles defends it off his back foot.
2 runs.
Length delivery on the fourth stump line, Alex leaves it alone.

Good stop by O'Shane Thomas. Length delivery on off, Hales drives it through point. Thomas comes running from third man and stops the ball from going to the fence with his big foot. The batsman meanwhile come back for the second.
Good length delivery on the stumps, Alex starts his innings by carefully blocking it off his back foot.
Jason Holder to bowl with the second new ball.
FOUR!!! Beautiful. Full length delivery on the pads. Bairstow effortlessly flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Jonny pushes it towards the fielder at mid on.

Cottrell pitches it on length on middle and le. The ball comes in towards Bairstow. He looks to defend but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal by the Windies player but the umpire turns it down. It looked going down the leg to the naked eye. The replays show that it would have been umpires call.
Yorker length delivery on off and middle, Bairstow gets his bat down in time and keeps it out.
Full length delivery on middle and off, Jonny pushes it towards mid off.
Good length delivery this time on the middle stump, Bairstow watchfully defends it.
Wide. Cottrell starts with a  length delivery down the leg side, Bairstow shoulders arms to it and the umpire stretches his arm to signal it as wide.
Finally everything is sorted and we are ready to get underway.
There is a slight delay in the start as there is ab issue with the sightscreen. The advertisement on the sightscreen is not turned off and they are trying to sort it out.

Players are out in the middle for the start of the 4th ODI. Alex Hales and Jonny Bairstow walk out to the middle to open the innings for the visitors. Sheldon Cottrell to take the first new ball for Windies.

England skipper, Eoin Morgan says that he hopes the team can bounce back like they have in the past. Says the wicket looks good. Ben Stokes replaces Jason Roy who has some niggle. On their fielding improvement Morgan says they are looking to maximize their potential and wants to add the extra dynamics before the World Cup by fielding better.

Windies skipper, Jason Holder says that he will field first as there is moisture on the pitch and hopes the fast bowlers can make early in roads at the start of the match. Expects the pitch to get better to bat later on. Says he is not concerned by the performance of the spinners as they have done well in  the past and expects them to come good.

Pitch Report - Darren Ganga with the pitch report says the maximum temprature will go to 29. Says there can be rain later on. On the 22-yard he says not much has been changed and the pitch scurrator has informed him that the roller was rolled yesterday. Says this is a fortress for Windies and have won all 5 matches here. Expects an even contest between the bat and ball. Adds that there will be spin on offer and a a bit of tennis ball bounce earlier. Teams winning the toss have opted to chase in the past and have done that successfully.
TOSS - Windies skipper, Jason Holder has won the toss and has elected to field first.

After rain played spoil sport in ODI no. 3, it is now time for ODI 4 at the same venue. The weather forecast is good today and let us hope that we can see a full game today. The series is nicely poised at 1-1 and a win here for any of the team will see them take an unassailable lead in this series. The Windies have momentum on their side after they won the last game but the visitors are still the favorites.
